New chimney construction begins with the fireplace or appliance the chimney will serve. The project must account for the proposed location, venting requirements, building structure, and connection to the roof.
Our team starts by reviewing the proposed chimney project, the property layout, and the intended fireplace or appliance.
For a new home, renovation, or fireplace addition, homeowners can provide building plans, appliance details, and the proposed installation location.

This information helps establish the starting requirements for the project.
The proposed chimney route must be compatible with the appliance and the building.
Important considerations include the chimney's location, required clearances, flue configuration, surrounding structure, and roofline.

The proposed arrangement must also allow for appropriate venting and weather protection.
Once the project requirements are understood, the proposed construction work can be defined.

Depending on the approved system, the scope may involve masonry construction, the chimney flue or liner, chimney termination, a crown or cap, and the connection where the chimney passes through the roof.

Fireplace installation, structural modifications, roofing work, and other trades must be identified separately when applicable.
Before construction proceeds, the project scope, responsibilities, required approvals, and applicable building requirements need to be established.
Santa Chimney Sweep reviews the proposed service with the homeowner so the agreed work and any separate responsibilities are clear.
Construction and completion requirements depend on the approved design, project conditions, and applicable local codes.

Not every chimney project requires a new structure. The right service depends on what already exists and what needs to change.
If your chimney is structurally serviceable but has localized cracks, water leaks, or damaged components, targeted repairs may be more appropriate than new construction.

[Explore Chimney Repair](https://www.santachimneys.com/services/chimney-repair/)
When an existing chimney has widespread masonry deterioration, loose sections, or other major damage, partial or complete rebuilding may be necessary.
Rebuilding an existing chimney is different from constructing a new chimney where none exists.

[Explore Chimney Rebuilding](https://www.santachimneys.com/services/chimney-repair/chimney-masonry-repair/chimney-rebuilding/)
If your main goal is to install a new fireplace or insert, the appliance type and venting requirements should be reviewed first.
Some appliances use approved venting systems that are different from a traditional masonry chimney.

[Explore Fireplace Installation](https://www.santachimneys.com/services/fireplace-installation/)
If your chimney already exists but you are changing the appliance or have concerns about the flue, an inspection can help establish whether the existing system is suitable.
A new chimney may not be necessary if an appropriate repair or venting modification can address the issue.
